newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PPC shares at year low on flat results.
newsitem.headline: PPC shares at year low on flat results.

text.p: Shares in Pretoria Portland Cement Ltd (PPC) on Friday slid to their lowest levels this year following the release of flat annual results and as the proposed merger of its competitors continued to dog the cement company.
Dealers said the worse-than-expected results had seen investors pull buying orders out of the market.
"With the disappointing results, buying orders have dried up," one dealer said, adding that there was little selling pressure on the share.
PPC on Thursday reported earnings before exceptional items unchanged at 464.8 cents a share, below analysts' consensus forecast of 489.7 cents.

Managing director John Gomersall blamed the poor performance on a decline in lime sales and an increase in the cement division's costs as new infrastructure was set up ahead of the disbandment of South Africa's cement cartel in September.
By 1215 GMT, PPC shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange had lost three percent or 200 cents to change hands at 66 rand. Volumes were very thin, with only 1,700 shares traded.
PPC's shares have been on a steady downward trend since the end of September and have fallen almost 40 percent since the beginning of the year when they touched this year's best level of 108 rand.
"South Africa's whole fixed investment side has not been performing well," another dealer said. "PPC is one of the harder hit as a result of this."

Traders said PPC shares had during the year been hurt by the proposed merger between two major competitors, Alpha Ltd and Blue Circle, a Murray and Roberts Holdings Ltd subsidiary, which would usurp its position as market leader.
Although South Africa's Competition Board has recommended to the Minister of Trade and Industry that the merger be blocked, a decision from the ministry is still outstanding.
